 Order

The petitioner- accused is before this Court seeking grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.PC in Crime No.17/2024 of Vishwanathapura Police Station, pending in Spl.C.C.No.290/2024 on the file of the learned Additional District and Sessions Judge (FTSC-III), Bengaluru Rural District,
Bengaluru, registered for the offences punishable under Sections 376(3) of IPC, Section 4(2) 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Section 9 of Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 and Section 3(2)(v) of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act, 1989, on the basis of the first information lodged by the informant Nagarathnamma.

sentences.text: 2. Heard Sri Srikanth B., learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Rahul Rai K., learned High Court Government NC: 2024:KHC:20938 Pleader for respondent No.1- State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 439 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioner being the sole accused is seeking grant of bail.
He was arrested on 29.01.2024 and since then he is in judicial custody.

Serious allegations are made against the petitioner that he induced the minor girl, aged below 16 years and married her by tying a thread around her neck and committed penetrative sexual assault forcibly.

The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that the parents of the victim girl informed the age of the victim as 18 years and therefore, the petitioner had married her cannot be accepted, NC: 2024:KHC:20938 since the school records Arjun vs State Of Karnataka By on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37544637/
2 produced by the prosecution along with the charge sheet discloses that the victim has not even attained 16 years of age at the time of the incident.
The medical records support the contention of the prosecution.

The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner that even the parents of the victim have taken part in the marriage of the petitioner with the victim cannot be a ground to dilute the seriousness of the offence committed by the petitioner.

Statement of the victim under Section 164 of Cr.PC was recorded by the learned Magistrate, wherein, the victim girl fully supported the case of the prosecution and stated about the offence committed by the accused forcibly.
The matter is pending for trial before the trial Court.
If at this stage, the petitioner is enlarged on bail, that will definitely terrorize the victim and other material witnesses.

5. Even though the medical records do not support the contention of the prosecution that penetrative sexual assault is committed by the petitioner forcibly, there are sufficient materials to support the contention of the prosecution that the petitioner has committed sexual assault after marrying the NC: 2024:KHC:20938 minor girl.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled for grant of bail.
6. Accordingly, petition is dismissed.
